paragraphs.text: Cap DSH desktop session cookie lifetime to avoid HTTP 431 / Web authentication failed startup crash.
修复 DSH 桌面端 dsh-auth-* cookie 累积导致的启动崩溃。
# dsh-cookie-guard

A tiny fix for **DeepSeek Harness Desktop**: it caps the lifetime of the desktop
browser-session coo

kies (`dsh-auth-*`) from the default 30 days to 7 days, so
stale cookies can no longer pile up and o

verflow the request header — a failure
that prevents the app from starting at all.

- Declarative bundle patch only; no runtime code, no changes to the installed app,
no Electron main-

process hacks.
- Survives app updates (it lives in your profile, not in `app.asar`).
- Ships a stand
alone cleanup script for machines that are already stuck.
## Symptom
At launch the app shows:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The diagnostic report (`%APPDATA%\@deepseek-ai\dsh-desktop\logs\crash-*-host.log`)
contains either:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
or the host logs an `HTTP 431` (Request Header Fields Too Large).
## Root cause
Not an account, network or plugin issue — it is unbounded cookie growth:

1. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-connection` names its cookie
`"dsh-auth-" + sha256(host:port)` — one coo

kie per authority, port included.
2. The Desktop Host always launches with `--port 0` (`main()` in
`

dsh-desktop-host`), so every start gets a new random port.
3. Cookies default to `cookieMaxAgeDays:

30` and nothing ever prunes them.
4. The Electron welcome page fetches with Chromium `net.fetch`, wh

ich sends
**every** historical `dsh-auth-*` cookie in one `Cookie` header.
5. Node's `maxHeaderSize`

defaults to 16 KB; one cookie is ≈200 B, so
**~90 cookies overflow the header**, the Host answers 4

31 and Electron throws
`desktop welcome: Web authentication failed`.

Measured: 71 cookies (~12 KB) accumulated in 13 days were enough to reproduce.
At 3–5 launches/day,

**any long-term desktop user hits this within a month**.
Web mode uses a fixed port and is unaffecte

d — this is desktop-only, present in
both `0.2.1-rc.3` and `rc.5`.

(`0.2.1-rc.3` and later).

Append `"dsh-cookie-guard"` to `dsh.profile.bundles` in the same `package.json`,
then restart DeepSe

h-cookie-guard"` to `dsh.profile.bundles` in the same `package.json`,
then restart DeepSeek Harness.
### Option 4 — cleanup only, no plugin
With DSH fully closed:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The script backs up `Network\Cookies`, then deletes every `dsh-auth-*` row.
The next launch issues a
fresh cookie and the app recovers.
## How it works
The package is just a bundle patch:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

DSH applies bundle patches after `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app`, so this overrides the
`connection` node

's config. A 7-day lifetime means at most "launches in 7 days"
cookies (< 35, ~7 KB), far from the 1

6 KB ceiling, while still covering sessions
that stay open for a week.

Use `1` for a tighter cap (daily restarts, but sessions older than a day expire);
increase it if you
keep the app open longer.
## Verify
After a restart:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Chromium timestamps are microseconds since 1601.
## Limitations

A plugin runs inside the Host process; it cannot read or delete the Electron
main process's Chromium

cookie store (exclusively locked at runtime). So a plugin
can only cap growth, not clean history. A

real fix belongs upstream — two minimal
options are in docs/upstream-issue.md:

1. Electron main: remove stale `dsh-auth-*` cookies before `host.start()`;
2. Connection service: na

me the cookie by host hash (`127.0.0.1`) so each start
overwrites the same cookie instead of adding

he cookie by host hash (`127.0.0.1`) so each start
overwrites the same cookie instead of adding one.
## Compatibility
| DSH Desktop | Status |

| 0.2.1-rc.3 | reproduces, patch works |
| 0.2.1-rc.5 | reproduces, patch works |
Desktop (packaged Windows/macOS) only; CLI / `dsh web` is unaffected.
